guarantees.definition: A leaf creation attempt succeeds only when the target name is absent at the atomic create operation; an existing target is never opened as the newly created object.
guarantees.scope: One regular-file leaf within an existing authority root.
limitations: Does not create a multi-file transaction.
Does not prevent non-cooperating actors from mutating the created file after the descriptor is closed.
guarantees.test_oracle: Concurrent create attempts for one absent leaf produce exactly one successful descriptor and all other attempts report an existing target without changing the winner bytes.

guarantees.definition: The authority can read bytes from the exact opened leaf descriptor and report a digest and length derived from those bytes.
guarantees.scope: A regular-file leaf descriptor opened or created by the authority.
limitations: Verification describes the bytes observed during readback and is not a perpetual integrity guarantee.
guarantees.test_oracle: Write known bytes through an authority descriptor and require descriptor readback digest and length to equal an independent digest and byte count.

guarantees.definition: Cooperating processes requesting the same target-root identity and lock scope are mutually excluded while the authority lock context is held.
guarantees.scope: One authority root identity and one exact lock-scope string within the implementation's declared local coordination domain.
limitations: Applies only to cooperating processes using the same authority implementation, scope, and coordination domain.
The profile must state when the coordination domain is narrower than one host.
guarantees.test_oracle: A second process cannot enter the same root-and-scope lock before the first process releases it, and can enter after release.

guarantees.definition: Leaf mutation is issued relative to pinned parent-directory descriptors and the authority detects replacement of every pinned namespace component before verification completes.
guarantees.scope: One relative locator beneath one opened authority root on a descriptor-relative filesystem API.
limitations: Does not constrain non-filesystem aliases outside the pinned namespace.
Requires every mutation path to use the pinned descriptors and to perform the binding assertion.
guarantees.test_oracle: Rename an opened parent and replace its former pathname; descriptor-relative mutation remains on the pinned parent, and namespace verification rejects the pathname replacement.

guarantees.definition: Replacing one regular-file leaf with another on the same mounted filesystem changes the destination name in one replace operation without exposing partially copied destination bytes.
guarantees.scope: Source and destination regular-file leaves on the same mounted filesystem supported by the authority implementation.
limitations: Does not make a multi-name transaction.
Does not imply durability after power loss.
guarantees.test_oracle: Concurrent observation during repeated replacement sees only complete old or complete new content, never a missing destination or partial content.

guarantees.definition: The authority can issue a synchronous namespace-metadata flush request for the pinned parent directory selected for a leaf mutation.
guarantees.scope: The pinned parent directory on a filesystem that accepts directory fsync.
limitations: Does not assert that any mutation mechanism calls this operation or establish ordering relative to file-content flushes.
The filesystem and storage stack define the ultimate power-loss durability semantics.
guarantees.test_oracle: Calling the authority operation issues fsync on the pinned parent directory descriptor, and a real writable target filesystem accepts the directory fsync call.
